endpoint.description: API base URL. Defaults to `https://api.noderings.com`. Can also be set with `NODERINGS_API_URL`.

http_timeout.description: Timeout for a single HTTP request, as a duration such as `60s`. Defaults to `60s`.

max_retries.description: How many times to retry rate-limited and transient failures. Defaults to `25`.

organization_id.description: Organization to act in, sent as `X-Organization-ID`. Defaults to the token's organization. Can also be set with `NODERINGS_ORGANIZATION_ID`.

requests_per_second.description: Client-side limit on requests per second for each API operation. Defaults to `2`, the API's own limit. Set `0` to disable.

skip_organization_check.description: Skip checking the token and organization when the provider is configured. Defaults to `false`.

token.description: Service-account token. Can also be set with `NODERINGS_TOKEN` (or `NODERINGS_API_TOKEN`, `NR_API_TOKEN`).

block.description: The NodeRings provider manages resources on the [NodeRings](https://noderings.com) cloud marketplace.

countries.description: Answers by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, for example `DE`.

default.description: Answer for resolvers that match no other rule.

name.description: Owner name relative to the zone, in lower case. Use `@` for the apex.

regions.description: Answers by ISO 3166-2 subdivision such as `US-CA`, or a region group such as `US-IX`.

ttl.description: Time to live in seconds, 30 to 60. Defaults to `60`.

type.description: Record type: A, AAAA, CNAME, NAPTR, SRV.

block.description: A geo-routed record: resolvers get an answer chosen by their location. The most specific match wins: region, then country, then continent, then `default`. Only one geo record per name is supported.

allow_overwrite.description: Take over records of this name and type that already exist in the zone. Without it, creating fails if they exist. Defaults to `false`.

name.description: Owner name relative to the zone, in lower case, for example `www` or `_dmarc`. Use `@` for the zone apex and `*` for a wildcard.

records.description: Record values in presentation format, for example `192.0.2.10`, `10 mail.example.com.` (MX) or `0 issue "letsencrypt.org"` (CAA). Write TXT values as plain text without surrounding quotes; long values are split for you. Hostnames should end with a dot.

ttl.description: Time to live in seconds, 30 to 86400.

type.description: Record type: A, AAAA, ALIAS, CAA, CERT, CNAME, DNAME, DS, HINFO, HTTPS, LOC, MX, NAPTR, NS, OPENPGPKEY, PTR, RP, SMIMEA, SRV, SSHFP, SVCB, TLSA, TXT.

block.description: All records of one name and type in a zone (an RRset). Use one resource per name and type, with every value in `records`.

delegation_ok.description: Whether the parent zone currently delegates to the NodeRings nameservers.

deletion_protection.description: When `true`, Terraform refuses to delete the zone. Defaults to `false`.

force_destroy.description: Delete the zone even while DNSSEC is active and the parent zone still has the DS record. That breaks resolution for validating resolvers until the DS is removed. Defaults to `false`.

name.description: Domain name, for example `example.com`. Stored lower-case without a trailing dot. Changing it replaces the zone. A domain can be hosted by only one organization at a time.

nameservers.description: Nameservers to set at the registrar.

state.description: `pending_ns` until the domain is delegated to NodeRings, then `active`.

block.description: A DNS zone hosted on NodeRings. After creating it, point the domain's nameservers at the `nameservers` output at your registrar.

ds.description: DS record to add at the registrar, as `<key tag> <algorithm> <digest type> <digest>`.

ds_at_parent.description: Whether the parent zone has the DS record.

force_destroy.description: Turn DNSSEC off even while the registrar still has the DS record. That breaks resolution for validating resolvers until the DS is removed. Defaults to `false`.

mode.description: `signed_ds_pending` until the DS is seen at the parent, then `signed_active`.

block.description: Signs a zone with DNSSEC. Add the `ds` value as a DS record at your registrar; the zone becomes `signed_active` once NodeRings sees it there.

key.description: Key: lower-case letters, digits and `_`. Unique in the organization. Changing it replaces the variable.

value.description: Value, 1 to 32767 characters. Changing it updates the variable in place.

block.description: An organization environment variable. Its value is not secret: anyone who can read the organization's variables can see it. Use `noderings_secret` for credentials.

cidrs.description: IPv4 and IPv6 CIDRs, for example `203.0.113.0/24` or `2001:db8::/48`. The API stores each one as its network address with IPv6 compressed (`192.0.2.5/24` becomes `192.0.2.0/24`); write them that way to match what other tools show. Use `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0` for every address.

name.description: Name, 1 to 63 characters, unique in the organization. Creating a virtual machine creates an address group named exactly like the VM's hostname, and later overwrites its CIDRs. Do not give a managed group the hostname of a virtual machine.

block.description:
A named list of CIDRs that firewall rules can use as a source or destination. Changes reach the virtual machines that use the group within about a minute.

Creating a virtual machine creates an address group named exactly like the VM's hostname, and later overwrites its CIDRs. Do not give a managed group the hostname of a virtual machine.

attached_vm_count.description: Number of virtual machines the ruleset is attached to.

attached_vm_hostnames.description: Hostnames of the virtual machines the ruleset is attached to, sorted.

force_destroy.description: Delete the ruleset even while virtual machines use it. The API then detaches it from those virtual machines, and the rules last applied to them may stay in effect until they get another ruleset. With the default `false`, Terraform refuses to delete an attached ruleset; detach it first.

name.description: Name, 1 to 63 characters, unique in the organization.

rule_count.description: Number of rules, ingress and egress together.

block.description: A firewall ruleset: a named, ordered list of rules that can be attached to virtual machines. Manage its rules with `noderings_firewall_ruleset_rules`. A new ruleset is empty, and an empty ruleset filters nothing: the default policy is to accept traffic in both directions. Only virtual machines on Proxmox support firewall rulesets.

ruleset_id.description: ID of the firewall ruleset. Changes in place: the old ruleset is detached, then the new one attached.

virtual_machine_id.description: ID of the virtual machine. Changing it replaces the attachment.

block.description:
Attaches a firewall ruleset to a virtual machine. A VM has at most one ruleset; use one attachment per VM.

Only platforms with the `guest_firewall` capability (Proxmox) support firewalls. Rule changes reach the VM within about a minute; the API does not report when they are applied.

The platform marks the VM as running when a ruleset is attached or detached. If the VM was stopped, this resource stops it again afterwards, so `power_state` on `noderings_virtual_machine` does not drift.

adopt_existing.description: When the ruleset already has rules at create time, take them over: rules that match a `rule` block are kept, the rest are deleted. With the default `false`, creating this resource fails if the ruleset is not empty, so an existing rule list is never replaced by accident. You can also import the rules instead.

ruleset_id.description: ID of the `noderings_firewall_ruleset`. Changing it replaces this resource.

destination_ports.description: Destination port: one port such as `443` or one range such as `8000-8100`. Lists are not supported; write one rule per port or range. Only for the protocols `tcp`, `udp`, `sctp`, `dccp`, `udplite`. Omit for any port.

direction.description: `ingress` (traffic to the virtual machine) or `egress` (traffic from it).

position.description: Position in the ruleset, starting at 0 (evaluated first).

protocol.description: IP protocol in lower case: `any`, `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `ipv6_icmp` (ICMPv6) and others. One of `tcp`, `udp`, `sctp`, `ipv6`, `icmp`, `icmpv6`, `esp`, `ah`, `ipsec`, `gre`, `ipip`, `vxlan`, `l2tp`, `geneve`, `any`, `igmp`, `ggp`, `ipencap`, `st`, `egp`, `igp`, `pup`, `hmp`, `xns_idp`, `rdp`, `iso_tp4`, `dccp`, `xtp`, `ddp`, `idpr_cmtp`, `ipv6_route`, `ipv6_frag`, `idrp`, `rsvp`, `skip`, `ipv6_icmp`, `ipv6_nonxt`, `ipv6_opts`, `vmtp`, `eigrp`, `ospf`, `ax_25`, `etherip`, `encap`, `pim`, `ipcomp`, `vrrp`, `isis`, `fc`, `mobility_header`, `udplite`, `mpls_in_ip`, `hip`, `shim6`, `wesp`, `rohc`.

source_ports.description: Source port: one port such as `443` or one range such as `8000-8100`. Lists are not supported; write one rule per port or range. Only for the protocols `tcp`, `udp`, `sctp`, `dccp`, `udplite`. Omit for any port.

address_group_ids.description: IDs of `noderings_firewall_address_group` resources. If every group and tag on this side stops resolving to an address (for example the virtual machine behind a hostname group was deleted), the platform skips the rule.

cidrs.description: IPv4 or IPv6 addresses or CIDRs. `0.0.0.0/0` (any IPv4) and `::/0` (any IPv6) must be the only entry on their side, with no other CIDRs, address groups or tags; to match both families, omit the block or write two rules.

vm_tags.description: Virtual machine tags, 1 to 100 characters each; they match the addresses of every virtual machine with the tag. Each tag must be on at least one existing virtual machine when the rule is written, so add `depends_on` for the virtual machines that carry it. If no virtual machine has the tag any more, the platform skips the rule.

block.description: Which addresses the rule matches as the destination. Set at least one of the arguments. Entries of different kinds are combined: the rule matches any of them. Omit the block to match any destination address.

address_group_ids.description: IDs of `noderings_firewall_address_group` resources. If every group and tag on this side stops resolving to an address (for example the virtual machine behind a hostname group was deleted), the platform skips the rule.

cidrs.description: IPv4 or IPv6 addresses or CIDRs. `0.0.0.0/0` (any IPv4) and `::/0` (any IPv6) must be the only entry on their side, with no other CIDRs, address groups or tags; to match both families, omit the block or write two rules.

vm_tags.description: Virtual machine tags, 1 to 100 characters each; they match the addresses of every virtual machine with the tag. Each tag must be on at least one existing virtual machine when the rule is written, so add `depends_on` for the virtual machines that carry it. If no virtual machine has the tag any more, the platform skips the rule.

block.description: Which addresses the rule matches as the source. Set at least one of the arguments. Entries of different kinds are combined: the rule matches any of them. Omit the block to match any source address.
A rule. Order matters: the first block is evaluated first. At most 50 rules per ruleset.

The rules of one firewall ruleset, as one ordered list. This resource is authoritative: it creates, updates, reorders and deletes rules so that the ruleset holds exactly the `rule` blocks in the configuration, in that order, and rules added outside Terraform show up as changes to remove. Use one `noderings_firewall_ruleset_rules` per ruleset.

Rules are evaluated top to bottom, ingress and egress in one list, and the first matching rule decides. Traffic that matches no rule is accepted, so for a default-deny policy end the list with `drop` rules for `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0`.

Changes reach the virtual machines the ruleset is attached to within about a minute; the API does not report when they are applied.

accept_eula.description: Accept the game's end-user licence agreement. Required when the game has one (`noderings_game_server_games.eula`). Only used when the server is created or its game changes. Not read back from the API.

allocation_limit.description: How many extra ports (allocations) the plan allows, besides the primary one.

allow_destructive_game_change.description: When `true`, changing `template_id` changes the game in place instead of replacing the server. The server keeps its address, but **all files, schedules and backups are deleted**. Defaults to `false`.

backup_limit.description: How many backups the plan allows.

database_limit.description: How many databases the plan allows.

deletion_protection.description: When `true`, Terraform refuses to delete the server. Defaults to `false`.

docker_image.description: Container image the game runs in. Must be one of the game's images (`noderings_game_server_startup.docker_images`). Changes in place.

environment.description: Startup variables, such as the game version or player limit. Only the keys listed here are managed; other variables keep their values. At creation, variables that cannot be edited may only be set to their default. Afterwards only user-editable variables can change. Keys are checked against the game's variables (see `noderings_game_server_games`). A change applies the next time the game starts: restart the server (for example by setting `power_state` to `offline` and back) to use it. Removing a key stops managing it; the server keeps its current value.

last_error.description: Why the last install failed, if it did.

name.description: Server name, 1 to 64 characters. Changes in place while the server is ready.

panel_identifier.description: Short server identifier shown in support conversations.

phase.description: `pending` while installing, `ready`, `error` (failed after payment; reinstall or change the game) or `failed` (failed before payment; delete it).

plan_id.description: Game-server plan ID. A server cannot move to another plan, so changing it replaces the server (its files are lost).

power_state.description: `running` or `offline`. When set, Terraform starts or stops the server and waits for it. When not set, it reports the live state. New servers start once installed.

region_id.description: Region to place the server in. Defaults to the region of the node the server is placed on. Changing it replaces the server.

template_id.description: Game to install, the `id` of a `noderings_game_server_games` entry. Game IDs are specific to the plan's provider. Changing it replaces the server, unless `allow_destructive_game_change` is `true`.

version_value.description: Game version to install, at most 64 characters. Only used when the server is created; to change the version later, set the game's version variable in `environment`. Not read back from the API.

create.description: How long to wait for create, as a duration such as `30m`. Defaults to `30m`.

delete.description: How long to wait for delete, as a duration such as `30m`. Defaults to `15m`.

update.description: How long to wait for update, as a duration such as `30m`. Defaults to `30m`.

block.description: Timeouts for long-running operations.

A game server ordered from a game-server plan. Creating it places an order that is billed according to the plan; Terraform waits until the game is installed. Destroying a fixed-price server forfeits the rest of the paid period.

alias.description: Host name alias for the IP, if any.

game_server_id.description: ID of the game server. Changing it replaces the resource.

notes.description: Free-form notes, for example what the port is for. Changes in place.

primary.description: Set to `true` to make this the server's primary address, the one players connect to. It cannot be set back to `false` directly: make another allocation primary instead. Destroying a primary allocation first makes the server's oldest other allocation primary.

block.description: An extra port (allocation) for a game server, for example a query or voice port. NodeRings picks the IP and port. Extra allocations count against the plan's `allocation_limit`. The server's own primary address is not managed by this resource; read it from `noderings_game_server.primary_ip` and `primary_port`. The game server must be ready.

game_server_id.description: ID of the game server. Changing it replaces the resource.

locked.description: Lock the backup so it cannot be deleted, for example by a scheduled backup task making room. Terraform unlocks it before destroying it. Defaults to `false`.

name.description: Backup name. Changing it creates a new backup and deletes this one.

create.description: How long to wait for create, as a duration such as `30m`. Defaults to `30m`.

block.description: Timeouts for long-running operations.

A backup of a game server's files. Terraform waits until the backup has finished. Backups count against the plan's `backup_limit`. Changing the server's game deletes all its backups; Terraform then creates this one again. Only the most recent backups (about 20) are listed by the API, so with more backups than that, older ones read as deleted. Restoring a backup is not done through Terraform. The game server must be ready.

connections_from.description: Hosts that may connect, as stored.

full_name.description: Database name as created, with the platform's prefix.

game_server_id.description: ID of the game server. Changing it replaces the resource.

jdbc_url.description: JDBC connection URL, including the password. Known under the same conditions as `password`.

name.description: Database name: letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to 48 characters. NodeRings adds a prefix (see `full_name`). Changing it replaces the database.

password.description: Password. Only known after create or rotation: after an import it is empty until `rotation_trigger` changes.

remote.description: Hosts that may connect, in MySQL notation. `%` (the default) allows any host. Changing it replaces the database.

rotation_trigger.description: Any value. Changing it sets a new random password. For example, set it to the current month to rotate monthly.

block.description: A MySQL database for a game server, for example for a plugin. Databases count against the plan's `database_limit`. The password is only returned when the database is created and when it is rotated; Terraform keeps it in state (marked sensitive). The game server must be ready.

active.description: Whether the schedule runs. Defaults to `true`.

day_of_month.description: Day of the month. Cron syntax; defaults to `*`.

day_of_week.description: Day of the week (0 or 7 is Sunday). Cron syntax; defaults to `*`.

cron.description: When the schedule runs, in the server's time zone.

game_server_id.description: ID of the game server. Changing it replaces the resource.

only_when_online.description: Run only while the server is running. Defaults to `false`.

action.description: `command` (send a console command), `power` (start, stop, restart or kill) or `backup` (create a backup).

continue_on_failure.description: Run the next tasks even if this one fails. Defaults to `false`.

payload.description: For `command`, the command to send. For `power`, one of `start`, `stop`, `restart` or `kill`. For `backup`, files to leave out of the backup, one pattern per line (optional).

time_offset.description: Seconds to wait after the previous task, 0 to 900. Defaults to `0`.

block.description: A step of the schedule. Tasks run in the order written; `time_offset` delays a task after the previous one.

A schedule that runs tasks on a game server at set times, for example a nightly restart or backup. Tasks run in the order they are written. Changing the server's game deletes all its schedules; Terraform then creates this one again. The game server must be ready.

description.description: Description. The API cannot clear a description, so removing this argument keeps the current one.

name.description: Name, 3 to 255 characters, unique in the organization (case-insensitive).

block.description: A group of users and service accounts. Manage its members with `noderings_group_membership` and its role with `noderings_role_assignment`.

group_id.description: ID of the group. Changing it replaces the resource.

service_account_ids.description: IDs of the service accounts in the group. An empty set removes every service account.

user_ids.description: IDs of the users in the group. An empty set removes every user.

block.description:
The members of one group. This resource is authoritative for each member type it sets: when `user_ids` is set, users not in it are removed from the group, and likewise for `service_account_ids`. A member type left unset is not managed. Use only one `noderings_group_membership` per group.

Users must already belong to the organization (they join through invites). Find their IDs with the `noderings_users` data source.

builtin.description: Always `false` for roles managed by this resource.

description.description: Description. The API cannot clear a description, so removing this argument keeps the current one.

name.description: Name, 3 to 255 characters, unique in the organization (case-insensitive).

permission_ids.description: IDs of the permissions the role grants. Look them up with the `noderings_permission` or `noderings_permissions` data sources. Permissions added outside Terraform are removed on the next apply.

block.description: A custom role: a named set of permissions that can be given to users, groups and service accounts with `noderings_role_assignment`. Built-in roles (Owner, Administrator, Billing, Operator, Viewer) are read-only; look them up with the `noderings_role` data source.

group_id.description: ID of the group that gets the role. Exactly one of `user_id`, `group_id` and `service_account_id` must be set. Changing it replaces the assignment.

role_id.description: ID of the role, custom or built-in. Changing it switches the principal to the new role in place.

service_account_id.description: ID of the service account that gets the role. Exactly one of `user_id`, `group_id` and `service_account_id` must be set. Changing it replaces the assignment.

user_id.description: ID of the user that gets the role. Exactly one of `user_id`, `group_id` and `service_account_id` must be set. Changing it replaces the assignment.

block.description: Gives a user, group or service account its role in the organization. Each principal has exactly one direct role, so applying this resource replaces any role the principal had, and destroying it leaves the principal with no direct role. Use one assignment per principal.

key.description: Key: lower-case letters, digits, `_` and `-`. Unique in the organization. Changing it replaces the secret.

value.description: Value, 1 to 255 characters. Changing it updates the secret in place.

block.description: An organization secret. The API never returns a secret's value, so Terraform cannot detect changes made to it outside Terraform. The value is stored in the Terraform state; protect the state accordingly.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 fingerprint as reported by NodeRings.

public_key.description: OpenSSH public key, for example the contents of `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`.

block.description: An SSH public key that virtual machines can be created with. Keys cannot be changed in place; changing any argument replaces the key.

additional_ipv4.description: Additional IPv4 addresses. Manage them with `noderings_virtual_machine_additional_ip`.

capabilities.description: Features the platform supports, such as `guest_firewall`, `on_demand_backup` and `snapshots`.

compliance_held.description: Whether the VM is held for a compliance review. A held VM rejects most changes.

coupon_code.description: Coupon to apply when ordering. Only used at create; later changes are ignored.

deletion_protection.description: When `true`, Terraform refuses to delete the VM, including for a replacement. Defaults to `false`.

distro.description: Operating system, one of `ubuntu_22_04`, `ubuntu_24_04`, `ubuntu_26_04`, `debian_12`, `debian_13`, `fedora_43`, `fedora_44`, `centos_9`, `centos_10`, `rocky_9`, `rocky_10`, `almalinux_9`, `almalinux_10`. See `data.noderings_distros`. Required unless `instant_app_id` is set; with an Instant App it defaults to the app's distro and must match it if set. Whether a provider has an image for a distro is only known at create. Changing it **replaces the VM** (a new VM, new IP addresses, a new subscription), or reinstalls it when `reinstall_on_change = true`.

firewall_ruleset_id.description: Attached firewall ruleset, empty if none. Manage it with `noderings_firewall_ruleset_attachment`.

has_active_backup.description: Whether the backup add-on is active. Manage it with `noderings_virtual_machine_backup`.

hostname.description: Hostname. Not unique: several VMs may share one. The platform also creates a firewall address group named after it, so don't name your own address groups after VM hostnames. Changing it **replaces the VM** (a new VM, new IP addresses, a new subscription), or reinstalls it when `reinstall_on_change = true`.

instant_app_id.description: Instant App to install, usually `data.noderings_instant_app.<name>.id`. Changing it **replaces the VM** (a new VM, new IP addresses, a new subscription), or reinstalls it when `reinstall_on_change = true`.

instant_app_slug.description: Slug of the Instant App installed at create or reinstall, if any.

instant_app_variables.description: Settings for the Instant App. Unknown names are rejected; see the `variables` of `data.noderings_instant_apps`. The API does not return them, so after import write them in configuration. Changing it **replaces the VM** (a new VM, new IP addresses, a new subscription), or reinstalls it when `reinstall_on_change = true`.

ipv4.description: Primary IPv4 address. On VirtFusion and SolusVM it can stay empty until the platform assigns one.

ipv6.description: Primary IPv6 address, empty if the region has no IPv6.

password.description: Root password, at most 255 characters. Stored in the Terraform state. The API does not return it, so after import write it in configuration. Changing it **replaces the VM** (a new VM, new IP addresses, a new subscription), or reinstalls it when `reinstall_on_change = true`.

plan_id.description: Plan to order, usually `data.noderings_marketplace_offer.<name>.plan_id`. Changing it **replaces the VM**: there is no resize.

power_state.description: `running` or `stopped`. Changes in place. If unset, Terraform does not manage the power state and only reports it. This is the requested state; the platform does not report the hypervisor's actual state.

region_id.description: Region of the plan, usually `data.noderings_marketplace_offer.<name>.region_id`. Changing it **replaces the VM**.

reinstall_on_change.description: When `true`, changes to `hostname`, `distro`, `instant_app_id`, `instant_app_variables`, `ssh_key_ids` or `password` **reinstall** the VM in place instead of replacing it. A reinstall keeps the VM, its IP addresses and subscription, but **wipes the disk, deletes all snapshots and cancels the backup add-on**. Defaults to `false`.

reinstall_status.description: State of the last reinstall: `none`, `requested`, `deleting`, `provisioning`, `completed` or `failed`.

reinstalled_at.description: Time of the last completed reinstall (RFC 3339).

ssh_key_ids.description: IDs of SSH keys (`noderings_ssh_key`) to install. Exactly one of `ssh_key_ids` and `password` is required. The API does not return them, so after import write them in configuration. Changing it **replaces the VM** (a new VM, new IP addresses, a new subscription), or reinstalls it when `reinstall_on_change = true`.

tags.description: Tags. Firewall rules can select VMs by tag. Changes in place. Tags starting with `tf-create-` are reserved.

create.description: How long to wait for create, for example `30m`.

delete.description: How long to wait for delete, for example `30m`.

update.description: How long to wait for update, for example `30m`.

block.description: How long to wait for operations to finish.

A virtual machine ordered from a provider on the NodeRings marketplace.

**Billing:** creating a VM starts a subscription for its plan. Destroying or replacing it cancels the subscription immediately with **no refund** for prepaid (monthly) plans; usage-billed VMs are charged for the final partial hour.

monthly_unit_price.description: Monthly price of the address, as a decimal string. Only known for addresses created by Terraform.

prorated_charge_amount.description: Amount charged when the address was added. Only known for addresses created by Terraform.

virtual_machine_id.description: ID of the virtual machine. Changing it replaces this resource.

block.description:
One extra IPv4 address for a virtual machine, from the same network as its primary address. A VM can have at most 10.

**Billing:** each address is a paid add-on. VMs on a monthly plan are charged a prorated amount when the address is added. Destroying this resource releases the address immediately; you may not get the same address back.

addon_id.description: Backup add-on, usually `data.noderings_marketplace_addon.<name>.id`. Changing it switches add-on in place; the old one is cancelled.

addon_status.description: Add-on status, `active` while backups are on.

virtual_machine_id.description: ID of the virtual machine. Changing it replaces this resource.

block.description:
Turns on the paid backup add-on for a virtual machine. The platform then takes backups on its schedule, starting with one right away; list them with `data.noderings_virtual_machine_backups`.

Only platforms with the `on_demand_backup` capability (Proxmox) support backups.

**Billing:** the add-on is charged on the VM's subscription. Destroying this resource cancels the add-on immediately and **deletes all of the VM's backups**. Reinstalling the VM also cancels it.

If the add-on is already active when this resource is created, it is adopted without enabling it again.

description.description: Description. Changing it replaces the snapshot.

name.description: Name the platform gave the snapshot.

operation_status.description: `completed` once the snapshot is taken, or `failed`.

status.description: `active` until the snapshot is deleted or expires.

virtual_machine_id.description: ID of the virtual machine. Changing it replaces the snapshot.

create.description: How long to wait for create, for example `30m`.

block.description: How long to wait for operations to finish.

**Experimental.** A snapshot of a virtual machine's disk. The NodeRings console does not show snapshots yet, so this resource may change in a later release.

Only platforms with the `snapshots` capability (Proxmox) support snapshots. Reinstalling or deleting the VM deletes its snapshots. Restoring a snapshot is not managed by Terraform.
